title: Koessler-2015-catching-10.1007/s10548-014-0417-z
description: Simultaneous scalp EEG and stereo-EEG (SEEG) recordings of interictal spikes originating from deep mesial temporal networks in seven patients with temporal lobe epilepsy. The dataset contains nine networks and 1945 one-second spike epochs centred on the earliest, highest-amplitude intracerebral spike. It supports study of how deep mesial temporal sources contribute to scalp EEG.
methods_description: Recordings used a 128-channel system at 512 Hz with an analog 0.15 Hz high-pass filter and a scalp FPz reference. Earliest high-amplitude interictal intracerebral spikes were marked at the peak of the initial component (t0). One-second epochs centred on t0 were band-pass filtered at 1.5-30 Hz without artifact rejection. Bipolar SEEG channels were stored together with scalp EEG channels.
